blocks.content: ETHAN

My plan for the day: finish coffee, find somewhere good to paint, make something decent enough to post online, maybe get a commission inquiry, definitely not spiral about whether freelancing at nineteen was a life plan or just an elaborate way to avoid having one. Normal Wednesday.
I packed my pencils. Mr. Alvarez materialized beside the table with a rag, though there was nothing near me that needed wiping. This is how he communicates that he's paying attention.

blocks.speaker: Mr. Alvarez
blocks.content: You are leaving early.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: Going to paint outside.

blocks.speaker: Mr. Alvarez
blocks.content: You say this like outside has done nothing to offend you.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: It has bugs. The light is good.
He glanced at the sketchbook. Said nothing. Which with Mr. Alvarez means everything.

blocks.speaker: Mr. Alvarez
blocks.content: New project?

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: Maybe.

blocks.speaker: Mr. Alvarez
blocks.content: Maybe is what artists say when they are afraid to admit they care.
I put the sketchbook in my bag.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: You always this encouraging?

blocks.speaker: Mr. Alvarez
blocks.content: I am a fountain of emotional support.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: You once told me my clouds looked like mashed potatoes.

blocks.speaker: Mr. Alvarez
blocks.content: They did. Emotionally supportive mashed potatoes.
I laughed and headed for the door.

blocks.speaker: Mr. Alvarez
blocks.content: Ethan.
I turned. He nodded toward the window — toward the street.

blocks.speaker: Mr. Alvarez
blocks.content: Sometimes a painting finds you before you find it.

blocks.speaker: Ethan
blocks.content: I have no idea what you mean.

blocks.speaker: Mr. Alvarez
blocks.content: That is only believable if I have recently suffered a head injury.
I grabbed my coffee and left before he could say anything else that was obviously correct.
